html:
The Gulidjan are an Aboriginal Australian people whose traditional lands cover the Lake Colac region of southwestern Victoria. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Their country took in grassland, woodland, volcanic plains and lakes east of Lake Corangamite, west of the Barwon River and north of the Otway Ranges. Neighbours included the Djargurd Wurrung to the west, the Girai Wurrung to the southwest and the Wathaurong to the north. Squatters moved onto Gulidjan land in the late 1830s, soon after the founding of Melbourne. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
